sections.html:
One office, the Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, does both jobs. It is open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, and the phone is 814-373-2537. Land records filed here include deeds, mortgages, mortgage satisfactions and releases, agreements such as oil and gas leases, UCC filings, notary publics and powers of attorney.

You can search records online back to 1954, and land records go back to 1800. For entries from 1954 through 1974, check the index books in the office. Written requests for copies cost $0.50 a page.

Owners can enroll in a free property fraud monitor built into the Landex software, which flags new filings recorded against the property.

Under the November 17, 2025 schedule, filing either a deed or a mortgage costs $74.75. Four pages and four indexed names are included; beyond that, add $0.50 per name and $2.00 per page.

Crawford County recording fees
Document or serviceRecording fee
Deed or mortgage$74.75
Mortgage satisfaction, release or assignment$59.75
Right of way, adverse possession, disclaimer$59.75
Plan map$43.50
Affidavit, agreement, power of attorney$18.50
Uniform Parcel Identifier, per parcel per document$20.00
Statement of Value$1.00
Copies or email, per page$0.50

Smaller items round out the list. A notary commission is $33.50, a declaration of taking is $10.00 plus $1.00 for each added page, a highway map is $16.50 plus $3.00 for each added page, and a UCC filing is $100.00. Faxed copies are $1.00 a page, a plan map copy is $10.00, and certifying a document is $1.50. A marginal notation is $2.00; it links a new document to an earlier one in the computer index and does not mark up the earlier document itself.

A payment that runs over by $5.00 or less is accepted and shown on the receipt as an overpayment. Mailing it in? Add a return envelope with at least $1.00 of postage, or a self-addressed stamped one. A fee calculator for the main recording documents is on the county website.

Any document the county ordinance covers must carry a Uniform Parcel Identifier number to be recorded. Each parcel numbered costs $20.00, due at recording and payable on one check together with the recording fee.

Your deed's parcel needs that number before the recorder takes the deed, so ask for it before closing day. No number yet? Ring 814-373-2537 and ask how to get the parcel numbered.

One change surprises some sellers: there is no separate check for the realty transfer tax anymore, so it can travel with the other payments. The state levies 1 percent of the value, buyer and seller share liability, and local governments frequently add their own.

sections.h2: How a Crawford County recording works, step by step
sections.html:
A typical sale unfolds in this order. The title agent or attorney drafts the deed and secures the UPI number for the parcel. At the closing table you sign with a notary present, and the buyer's address is added. The agent then adds up the recording fee, UPI fee, any Statement of Value charge and transfer tax, and submits everything on paper or through an e-recording company.

After acceptance the document is indexed and the buyer appears in the searchable records. Selling without a title company? Phone 814-373-2537 to confirm the total, then carry a check for the full sum, because a wrong amount can hold the package up.

Keep copies of the signed deed and the receipt for your own records, since the recorded copy can be ordered later at $0.50 a page. Timing matters as well. The counter closes at 4:30, so plan your drop-off with some margin on a closing day.

Four electronic recording companies are on the county's list, so a title company can usually send a deed without a courier.

  • Simplifile, at 800-460-5657 or simplifile.com.
  • EPN, at 888-325-3365.
  • CSC, at 866-652-0111 or erecording.com.
  • Indecomm Global Services, at 877-272-5250.

E-recorded Statement of Value forms carry a small added charge. Any document attached to the form costs $0.50 per page, and the system calculates the amount automatically.

sections.h2: Selling a house held by an estate
sections.html:
The Register of Wills sits in the same office, so an heir can open the estate and later record the deed in one place. This office probates estates, collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax and takes the resident inheritance tax returns. Opening an estate takes a death certificate and a $7.00 filing fee.

  • Every estate on file is public record, and estate records from 1991 to the present are online.
  • Probated estates go back to 1800, including most of the old original wills and supporting papers.
  • Will indexes cover 1800 to 1974 and 1975 to 2000.
  • Copies mailed or faxed on written request are $0.50 a page plus fees.

Once the estate has authority to sell, the sale follows the normal recording steps, including the UPI number and a Statement of Value when the transfer is not a paid sale.

The county's estimated population was 81,792 in July 2025, down 2.6 percent from the 2020 base. Meadville is the county seat and the largest city, with Titusville the other city. There are 42,385 housing units, and 74.7 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owned home is $153,200, the median monthly rent is $802, and median household income is $60,476. The county issued 99 building permits in 2025.

The 2020 census counted 42,063 housing units, and 19.3 percent of them were vacant. That is a lot of empty housing, so expect buyers to compare your listing with plenty of other choices. Lakeside areas around Pymatuning Reservoir and Conneaut Lake bring a seasonal market of their own.

A tidy package keeps the deed from bouncing.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the buyer's address.
  • The UPI number for the parcel and $20.00 to cover the fee.
  • A check for the recording fee from the November 17, 2025 schedule, with state and local transfer tax.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or not paid in full.
  • Postage and a return envelope for mailed packages.

Recording comes last, but the tax and fee amounts depend on the sale price, so ask the title agent to work out the totals in advance. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, yet the deed still needs the same parcel number, notary block and payment before it can go on record.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a Crawford County deed?
faqs.a: A deed is $74.75 under the schedule effective November 17, 2025, covering four pages and four names. Extra names are $0.50 each and extra pages $2.00 each.

faqs.q: What is the UPI fee in Crawford County?
faqs.a: It is $20.00 for each parcel that receives a number, paid when the document is recorded. The fee can go on the same check as the recording fee.

faqs.q: Does Crawford County want a check just for transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The office no longer requires separate checks for the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax.

faqs.q: Can a Crawford County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, EPN, CSC and Indecomm Global Services are the listed electronic recording companies.

faqs.q: How far back can I search Crawford County records online?
faqs.a: Recorder of Deeds records are online from 1954 to the present, and land records exist back to 1800. For 1954 to 1974, check the index books in the office.
